name_en: Mettajiru — pork and root vegetable miso soup with sweet potato
summary_ja: さつまいもや大根、人参など根菜をたっぷり入れた豚汁で、じゃがいもではなくさつまいもを使うのが特徴とされる。「やたらめったら具を入れる」が名の由来ともいわれ、家庭ごとに味が違う。
summary_en: A pork and root vegetable miso soup loaded with sweet potato in place of the more common potato — its name, roughly "every which way," is said to nod to the habit of throwing in whatever vegetables are at hand, so the taste shifts from home to home.
source_title: めった汁 石川県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Bekanabe — herring pickled in rice bran, simmered in a hot pot
summary_ja: ぬか漬けにしたイワシ（コンカイワシ）を、白菜やきのこと酒粕で煮込む能登の冬鍋。冷蔵技術のない時代の保存食が発祥とされ、大衆魚だったことから「今日も食べっか」が名の由来ともいわれる。
summary_en: Sardines pickled in rice bran are simmered with napa cabbage, mushrooms, and sake lees in this Noto winter hot pot, said to descend from a preservation method from before refrigeration — its name reputedly a nod to how commonly the cheap fish was eaten.
source_title: べか鍋 石川県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Itokojiru — azuki bean and tofu miso soup
summary_ja: 小豆と豆腐、根菜を味噌汁仕立てでじっくり煮る。親鸞聖人の命日に営む報恩講の膳に欠かせないとされ、好物だったという小豆を食べながら恩に報いるという意味が込められているという。
summary_en: Azuki beans, tofu, and root vegetables are slow-simmered into a miso-based soup, said to be essential at the memorial gathering for the founder of Jodo Shinshu Buddhism on his death anniversary — eating the beans, his favorite, is meant as a gesture of gratitude.
source_title: いとこ汁 石川県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Megisu no dangojiru — icefish fishcake dumplings in broth
summary_ja: 骨を抜いてすり身にしたメギスに味噌や卵、ねぎを混ぜてだんごにし、出汁で煮る。漁獲量全国トップとされる石川で、大漁に獲れるメギスを使い切る知恵として根づいたと伝わる。
summary_en: Icefish, deboned and ground into a paste with miso, egg, and scallion, are shaped into dumplings and simmered in dashi — said to have taken root as a way to use up a fish Ishikawa catches more of than anywhere else in the country.
source_title: メギスのだんご汁 石川県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Ishiru nabe — hot pot seasoned with Noto's fish sauce
summary_ja: 能登に伝わる魚醤いしるを出汁に使い、旬の魚介と野菜を煮る冬の鍋。少なくとも1700年代には作られていたとされ、秋田のしょっつる、香川のいかなご醤油と並ぶ発酵調味料が土台になっている。
summary_en: Noto's traditional fish sauce, ishiru, forms the base for this winter hot pot of seasonal seafood and vegetables — said to have been made since at least the 1700s, built on a fermented seasoning ranked alongside Akita's shottsuru and Kagawa's ikanago shoyu.
source_title: いしる鍋 石川県｜うちの郷土料理
